account:
Something may be being arranged informally, but I do not yet know what. At tea, my neighbour said Townsfolk 02 had reported lights or decorations at the bakery. This is secondhand and unconfirmed: the neighbour had asked the baker, who knew of no special occasion. My neighbour also heard the builder calling for a private meeting with the innkeeper. I have heard the builder shouting myself, but could not make out the words, so I cannot independently confirm the subject. These details might point to preparations for a gathering or celebration, but could equally be ordinary business or a misunderstanding; I have no evidence that they are connected or deliberately being concealed from me.

The innkeeper requested a meeting with me tomorrow at eighteen in the great hall about an inn matter. I accepted, and the secretary has recorded it as confirmed, although my acceptance has not yet been delivered to him. He is now visible walking near the plaza. I do not know whether his business relates to the builder or the decoration talk.

I have kept today's appointments, including tea, and returned for afternoon office hours. The secretary says the appointment books are secure. No specific account papers were supplied for our accounts appointment, and the secretary found the four great hall tables empty. Neither of us knows who last handled the accounts. That is an unresolved administrative issue, not evidence of a plot. I have asked the secretary to stop searching without a lead and to tell me whether anyone needs my attention. The best lead for understanding the unusual chatter is the original report from Townsfolk 02, or a straightforward conversation with the builder or innkeeper.
